title: GCP ACE vs AWS SAA-C03: Google or Amazon Cloud?
subtitle: Choosing your first associate cloud cert based on the job market and your profile

pros: Fewer candidates = less competition — a certified GCP profile stands out more easily.
A focus on IAM + Kubernetes (GKE) that is highly valued at cloud-native companies and SaaS startups.
Only $125 — cheaper than the AWS SAA-C03 ($150).
BigQuery, Vertex AI, GKE — a stronger data & ML positioning than Azure or AWS.
cons: A smaller market than AWS — GCP roles are ~15-20% of cloud job postings in France vs ~50% for AWS.
Fewer free prep resources than AWS (less GCP content on Udemy/YouTube).
The exam is reputed to be harder than the AWS CLF, but opinions differ on how it compares to the SAA-C03.
certs.bestFor: You're targeting cloud-native companies, SaaS startups or data/ML clients. You want to stand out in a less saturated market than AWS.

pros: The #1 cloud cert worldwide — the largest pool of job openings, in France and across Europe.
A strong résumé signal: IT recruiters know the SAA-C03, not always the GCP ACE.
Huge prep resources: Andrew Brown, Stéphane Maarek, Tutorials Dojo — unbeatable support.
AWS holds ~33% of the global cloud market — a high chance AWS is in your next employer's stack.
cons: $150 for the exam — slightly more than the GCP ACE.
A more saturated market: lots of AWS profiles → harder to stand out at an equivalent level.
AWS architecture (VPC, IAM, EC2, S3, RDS, etc.) + pricing = a broad scope, ~80-120 hours of realistic prep.
certs.bestFor: You're looking for your first full-time cloud job, you want the most recognized cert, or you're targeting IT services firms / large enterprises that mostly run on AWS.

verdicts.profile: You're looking for your first full-time cloud job and want to maximize the number of openings.
verdicts.why: AWS dominates the job market. The SAA-C03 opens the largest pool of openings — all the more so because non-technical recruiters recognize it instantly.

verdicts.profile: You're targeting data-first companies, SaaS startups or ML/AI teams.
verdicts.why: GCP is the reference cloud for BigQuery, Vertex AI and Looker. These teams look for GCP profiles, not AWS. The GCP ACE opens that niche, where you'll be rare.

verdicts.profile: You're already a Linux admin or SRE and want to move into cloud.
verdicts.why: GCP inherits from the Linux/GKE world: resource-oriented IAM, Compute Engine close to bare metal, native GKE. The transition is smoother than AWS if you come from a Linux ops background.

verdicts.profile: You work at an IT services firm / consultancy with a varied client base.
verdicts.why: Most large enterprises have AWS in their cloud stack. The SAA-C03 makes you directly billable on projects — the GCP ACE is a rare bonus, but not a versatile foundation at a consultancy.
The GCP ACE costs $125 vs $150 for the SAA-C03. If budget is the constraint, that's $25 saved on an exam that stays highly valued in its ecosystem.

tldr: AWS SAA-C03 if you want the largest job market and a universally recognized résumé signal. GCP ACE if you're targeting data/ML or SaaS startups, or want to stand out in a less saturated segment. Budget: the GCP ACE costs $25 less.
